ov.title: Marketing
ov.sub: From ad money to real profit. Every figure uses delivered orders, not just placed ones.
ov.kProfitSub: after product, courier, COD, packet and ads
ov.eyeNone: Nothing urgent — every campaign is paying.
ov.daily: Spend vs delivered sales per day
ov.rule: Verdict rule (change it in Rules): {scale}+ sales per {cur}1 = Scale, {keep}+ = Keep, {fix}+ = Fix, below = Stop.
ov.aiBest: {name} brings the most profit after ads ({profit}).
ov.aiWeak: {name} is the weakest ({per} per {cur}1) — change the audience or photos, or cut the budget.
ov.aiNone: No ad spend in this period yet.

ac.title: Ad campaigns
ac.sub: Every platform in one table. Tap a campaign to see inside it.
ac.empty: No campaign on this platform yet.

why.SCALE: Brings {per} for every {cur}1 — give it more budget.
why.KEEP: Pays well ({per} per {cur}1). Test new photos to grow.
why.FIX: Weak ({per} per {cur}1). Change audience or photos, or cut budget.

ac.note: “Profit after ads” = delivered sales − product cost, courier, COD fee, packet and return cost − ad spend. Website orders from an ad link count fully; Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp orders count by the channel rules in Settings.

mc.title: Message campaigns
mc.sub: SMS and WhatsApp offers to your own customers — the cheapest sales you can get.
mc.risk: {n} customers have not ordered in {days}+ days. A "we miss you" message to them is the cheapest sale you can make.
mc.autosSub: Sent by themselves at the right moment
mc.autosNote: The wording of each message is in Settings › Customer messages.

au.title: Audiences
au.sub: Customer groups built from your own orders. Use them for messages, or send them to Meta and Google to find people like them.
au.kRefusedSub: Left out of every ad and message
au.guide: Only customers who agreed to messages get them. Phone numbers are sent to Meta and Google in locked (hashed) form; they never see the numbers themselves.

cal.title: Marketing calendar
cal.sub: Holidays, offers, ads and messages on one calendar, so nothing big comes as a surprise.
cal.prepared: Ads or an offer are already planned before it.
cal.notPrepared: Nothing is planned for the 2 weeks before it yet — plan stock, ads and an SMS now.
cal.clash: “{a}” and “{b}” overlap — customers may stack both.

pl.title: Plan & ideas
pl.sub: Next month’s budget, where to spend, what to post, what others are doing — and AI suggestions waiting for your OK.
pl.districtNone: Not enough orders by district in this period yet.
pl.ideasBody: Photo, video and post ideas made from your products. Nothing goes live until you approve it.
pl.compSub: From their public ad library pages, checked weekly
pl.compBody: What the other shops run, from their public ad pages.

tl.title: Ad accounts
tl.sub: Which ad platforms are linked, and whether they can see your sales correctly.

ib.title: Inbox
ib.sub: {open} open · {un} not assigned · first reply in {avg} on average · longest wait {wait}
ib.viewNoteMsgs: Messenger, WhatsApp, Instagram and website chat
ib.unassignedNote: {n} chats have no owner. Assign them so nobody waits.
ib.allAssigned: Every open chat has an owner.
ib.pick: Pick a conversation on the left

st.title: Response times
st.sub: How fast customers hear back. Every hour a buyer waits, the chance of an order drops.
st.peak: Most orders come around {h}:00–{h2}:00 — keep someone on chat then.
st.byHourSub: Customer messages, by hour of the day
st.ordHourSub: Plan chat staff around these hours

fn.title: Finance
fn.asOf: Where your money is, as of {at}

sn.title: Profit snapshot
sn.sub: Green = what you keep, orange = what it cost
sn.open: Open Profit & loss for this period
sn.vsMonth: vs the same number of days before
sn.note: Net profit after every cost. Monthly fixed costs (rent, salaries) are spread per day, so "Today" is fair. Tap a number to open Profit & loss for that period.

ms.title: This month so far
ms.foot: {from}–{to} · sales counted on delivery date · same numbers as Home and Reports.

dec.title: Decide today
dec.sub: Each card has one action. Done cards disappear.
dec.claimText: {amt} still to receive. Chase them before the next statement.
dec.vatText: While it is off, no VAT line shows anywhere in Finance.
dec.lineText: {amt} less than our books. Claim it before the next statement.
dec.erpHead: Pay the ERP {amt} to stay safe
dec.erpText: Owed {owed}. Last payment {d} days ago; orders stop after {left} more days without a payment.
dec.adText: Your target is {target}%. Ads so far this month: {ads}.

fp.sub: Line by line. A sale counts on the day it is delivered.
fp.note: {n} delivered. Fixed costs spread per day. Same maths as Home and Reports.

close.title: Close the month
close.sub: Locks the month and sends its summary to the ERP.

drill.title: Where the profit comes from
drill.sub: Profit after ads, by the channel each order came from.
drill.insight: {best} brings {pct}% of this profit. Lowest margin: {worst} at {m}%.
drill.empty: No delivered order in this period.

fp.moreLink: More: lines, day by day, money report

refunds.title: Wallet & refunds
refunds.sub: Money we owe customers: wallet balance and refunds of prepaid orders.

vat.sub: VAT included in your sales, month by month.

budgets.title: Costs & budgets
budgets.sub: Fixed costs record themselves; you add the rest with a receipt.

wl.walletNote: {n} customers · they spend it on next orders
wl.monthNote: Only prepaid orders. No cash refund after delivery.
wl.none: No customer holds wallet money now.
wl.exchangeNote: {n} · added after the old piece passes the check

of.title: Offers & discounts
of.sub: Every way a customer can pay less or get more: one place to see what runs, what it costs and what it earns.

seg.allD: Everything customers can get: codes, automatic discounts, free delivery, rewards and points.
seg.couponsD: Customers type a code at checkout.
seg.autoD: No code needed. Sale prices and automatic offers show by themselves.
seg.shipD: Delivery charge taken off. The basic Free delivery rule is under "Built-in rules" below.
seg.onlineD: A reward for paying by bKash, Nagad or card: free delivery, % or ৳ off, points or wallet credit.
seg.pointsD: Rewards that are given back later, not taken off the price now.
seg.abandonedD: Used in Incomplete orders messages and by the AI follow-up to bring people back.
seg.firstD: Offers only for new customers, or only for people who already bought.

of.costNote: Cost = discount given. Click a row for the full picture.
of.kMarginNone: not known until every item has its buying price

aw.title: Awaiting your approval
aw.sub: Nothing goes live until you approve with your PIN.

hd.title: Heads up
hd.sub: Offers that could apply to the same cart.
hd.none: No overlaps. Every cart gets at most one discount.
hd.pair: "{a}" and "{b}" both change the same thing ({slot}). One of them wins; check which.

cal.title: Calendar
cal.sub: Next 5 weeks. The dark line is today.

wz.credit: The customer can use it on the next purchase.
wz.pointsHint: Set the value of a point in Customers › Loyalty.

mn.handSub: Cash, bank, bKash and Nagad together
mn.handNone: The cashbook is not set up for you to see.
mn.couriersSub: {n} delivered parcels not paid yet · oldest {d} day(s)
mn.couriersNone: No delivered parcel waits for money.
mn.erpPaid: Paid {d} days ago · orders stop in {left} days without a payment
mn.erpLate: No payment for {d} days · orders stop in {left} days
mn.erpHold: Orders are on hold until you pay
mn.erpNoDate: What the shop owes the ERP for the pieces it sells
mn.erpOff: The ERP link is not set up yet
mn.walletsSub: Money we owe {n} customers (they spend it on next orders)

cm.title: Courier money
cm.sub: One claims list for the whole shop: raise it here or in Orders, it shows everywhere.
cm.noPayout: No payout is expected right now.

fc.title: Next {n} days of cash
fc.fixed: Fixed costs due in this time: {amt}.
fc.none: No forecast yet. The cashbook has to be on and visible to you.
fc.start: Start: {amt} in hand. Courier cash arrives evenly, then the fixed costs go out. A guess, never a promise.

bm.title: Books match with the ERP
bm.bad: Not matching. Our books: {ours} · ERP says: {erp} · {n} line(s) to fix.
bm.good: Matching. Both say {amt}. Daily summary sent every night.
bm.off: The ERP link is not set up yet, so there is nothing to match.
